items.title: Show HN: Coding agent skills, tested on 15 backend tasks with hidden checks
items.story_key: story|title:coding agent skills tested on 15 backend tasks with hidden checks
items.content_excerpt: Skills that stop AI agents from writing backend code that passes the demo and breaks in production. Critical mistakes: 25/150 runs without, 2/150 with. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor. Agent skills that make Claude Code, Codex and Cursor write backend code like a senior engineer: safe on auth, data, money and schema changes by default. We gave agents 15 backend tasks with and without the skills, then ran a hidden check the agent never sees: 20 buyers at once for 5 items in stock, a user reading someone else's order, the old app version running against the new schema mid-deploy. Critical mistakes: 25/150 runs without the skills, 2/150 with them. (Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, 5 runs per task.) Runs with a critical mistake, without → with the skills. Missed team conventions (down migrations, API docs) went from 30 to 4. Not fixed yet: Haiku on out-of-order webhook events. Every raw run, the tasks and how to rerun it are in bench/ . Codex and other AGENTS.md agents: append dist/AGENTS.md . Cursor: copy dist/cursor/ into .cursor/rules/ . Each skill ends with a Make it yours section for your team's choices (error format, API docs). Left as "not set", the agent follows what your repo already does. Agent still made a mistake with the skills loaded? Open an issue with the prompt and the diff. Edit skills in skills/ , then node scripts/build-dist.mjs . Skills that stop AI agents from writing backend code that passes the demo and breaks in production. Critical mistakes: 25/150 runs without, 2/150 with. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor.

items.title: APM – A dependency manager for AI agents
items.story_key: story|title:apm a dependency manager for ai agents
items.content_excerpt: APM is a dependency manager for AI agents. Declare the skills, prompts, instructions, plugins, and MCP servers your project needs in one apm.yml , then any developer runs apm install to deploy each primitive to the harnesses that support it. See the targets matrix for support across GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Grok Build, Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, Gemini, Windsurf, and Kiro. One apm.yml across supported harnesses and machines. The lockfile pins exact versions and content hashes so a fresh clone resolves the same package content byte-for-byte. Every install scans for hidden Unicode, pins content hashes, and blocks transitive MCP servers unless they are explicitly declared or trusted. No opt-in required. apm-policy.yml is enforced at install time, including transitive MCP. Tighten-only inheritance flows enterprise -> org -> repo. Runtime behavior is your harness’s domain. See the Governance Guide . Homebrew is optional. See all installation options for pip, Scoop, and manual installs. For standalone Unix installs, follow the installer’s shell-specific PATH guidance if the current terminal cannot find apm . This example omits $schema and uses APM’s working-draft contract. For an explicit schema, see contract selection and the corrected schema candidate ; the older published schemas reject the Git-plus-path form shown below. That’s it. Each selected harness receives the primitives it supports in one command; every dependency is pinned, and every MCP server is policy-checked before it touches disk. Install someone else’s primitives and run them on your harness. Start in the consumer ramp . Build skills, prompts, plugins, or full packages others can install. Start in the producer ramp . APM is open source under the microsoft org, MIT-licensed. Built on AGENTS.md , Agent Skills , MCP . See the changelog for what shipped recently.

items.title: AI Source Code Analysis Detection Evasion Techniques
items.story_key: story|title:ai source code analysis detection evasion techniques
items.content_excerpt: This post investigates whether the source code of a program can be presented so that a large language model based analysis fails to report a defect that is genuinely present even though the models know what exception they miss (i.e. they have the knowledge but they don't apply it). Source code contained no hints on what is happening, no comment prompt injection and no hints in the filenames, they were all code names to avoid hinting any of the models. Here we are explaining a C-to-C transformation that hides a planted stack buffer overflow (bugdoor) from four frontier AI models (Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, OpenAI GPT-5.5, Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5). The tool used for this research was Karma Pro ( https://reviewcode.org ). Each model scanned the code at least 3 times. The interesting part: Some models knew the tricks we used but they still missed identifying the vulnerabilities However if I ask, some of the models know they missed the planted vulnerability but they could not reason to it. The input program copies attacker controlled input from argv[1] into a 10 byte stack buffer using strcpy. The transformed program performs the exact same bytes write operation, but hides the unbounded length behind two techniques: It prints the supplied name. strcpy copies bytes until it hits a null terminator (\0). If argv[1] is 11+ bytes, strcpy writes past buffer[10], corrupting the stack. This is a stack buffer overflow . Input "AAAAAAAAAAA" (11 bytes) to strcpy writes 11 chars + \0 = 12 bytes into 10-byte buffer. Bytes 10 and 11 overflow into frame pointer and return address. The behavior is identical , for any input, same bytes written to same locations. Overflow still at 10 bytes. strcpy is a single library call, pattern matchable. The loop forces the model to trace k. strlen returns length n. strcpy writes n + 1 bytes. Our loop writes k chars + terminator at buffer[k] = k + 1 bytes. When k = n, identical to strcpy. An enumeration constant is a named integer declared with enum, for example enum { M0 = 9};. The compiler knows its value. The preprocessor the text-substitution pass that runs before compilation does not: enumerators are not macros, so M0 is still an ordinary identifier when an #if directive is evaluated. The C standard discusses this in two steps. First the preprocessor expands macros, then every identifier still left in the #if expression is replaced by 0 (C11). items.title: Project EVE: Claude plays MMORPGs
items.summary: We put Claude in two EVE games to study how AI agents handle markets and teamwork, where they break down, and what safeguards they might need.
items.content_excerpt: This post shares research done as part of the Anthropic Fellows Program, April–July 2026. AI models may one day participate in real companies and markets, and several of our projects explored what that might look like. Claude has run a shop in our office , haggled on behalf of colleagues , and written code to fly a drone . In this project, we turned to a different setting: massively multiplayer online role-playing games (MMORPGs). MMORPGs are virtual worlds that in many ways reflect the complexity of the real world. They feature campaigns that coordinate many players, the acquisition and management of scarce resources, orienting and navigating through space, and trading in intricate in-game economies, all in a low-stakes environment. Doing all of this over weeks and months sits right at the edge of what frontier language models can currently do. We partnered with Fenris Creations to have Claude play two games in the EVE Universe: EVE Online, which has run continuously for more than two decades, and EVE Frontier, which is newer and still in development. Both are science-fiction games in which players fly spaceships around the vast galaxy, exploring, trading and fighting. In each, everyone shares one universe, and nearly everything of value in it is gathered and built by the players themselves, through long supply chains. Players can cooperate or betray each other, so getting anywhere takes organization and trust, much as it does in a real company. In EVE Online, the older of the two, this design has led to corporations and alliances whose campaigns coordinate hundreds of players over many months, and a history that includes megaprojects , war economies , tax havens , and elaborate corporate infiltration . In EVE Online, the first of the two games, Claude played as a lone trader, instructed only to maximize profit, in a simulated rerun of an in-game market. Newer models made consistent profits where simple algorithmic strategies lost money. The average earnings tripled from Claude Opus 4.6, the oldest model we tested, to Claude Fable 5, the newest. Nearly all models relied on the same low-risk strategy of buying items and reselling them for slightly more. When we asked them to bet on where prices were heading, even Fable 5 made money in only about half of its runs. items.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
items.summary: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.

items.title: Migrating vLLM to the LibTorch Stable ABI
items.summary: How vLLM migrated its CUDA build and compiled dependencies to the LibTorch Stable ABI, enabling compatible PyTorch upgrades without rebuilding vLLM.
items.story_key: model:vllm|title:migrating vllm to the libtorch stable abi
items.content_excerpt: vLLM relies heavily on PyTorch, with frequent calls to LibTorch in its C++ backend. As a result, changes to LibTorch’s binary interface may require vLLM to be rebuilt and relinked, even when the APIs remain unchanged. What if we could update LibTorch without rebuilding vLLM? That’s where the LibTorch Stable ABI comes in. With a LibTorch Stable ABI, updating LibTorch does not require rebuilding or updating vLLM in order to keep using it. Instead, we could swap out the torch wheel and import it directly into our vLLM package. As of v0.33.0, vLLM publishes LibTorch ABI Stable CUDA wheels. Left: Unstable ABI—new torch requires vLLM to rebuild. Right: Stable ABI—vLLM can import new torch directly. Note: Compatibility between vLLM and PyTorch still depends on other factors, including Python APIs, GPU-related requirements (such as the minimum supported CUDA version), and third-party dependencies. The LibTorch Stable ABI addresses binary compatibility but does not eliminate these other constraints. An application binary interface (ABI) defines how compiled code interacts with a library: how functions are called, data is laid out, and symbols are named. Even if an API looks the same in source code, an ABI change can force extensions to rebuild. A stable ABI preserves a supported set of binary interfaces across compatible versions, so extensions that use them can keep working without a rebuild. PyTorch's LibTorch Stable ABI has three layers: a stable C shim exposing selected LibTorch APIs, C++ wrappers that make the shim easier to use, and headeronly utilities in torch::headeronly that do not link against libtorch.so . Before the Stable ABI, a new PyTorch release could require a vLLM rebuild, delaying support for the new version and its features. With the Stable ABI, the same vLLM wheel can work across compatible PyTorch releases, letting users upgrade sooner and reducing rebuilds for package distributors. For developers, this means you can update and rebuild PyTorch, then test those changes in vLLM without rebuilding vLLM. Left: vLLM needs to change as LibTorch changes. Right: vLLM can change independent of LibTorch. The LibTorch Stable ABI is a limited subset of all of LibTorch. While many common ops are already supported through the C shim and through the higher level C++ convenience wrappers, not all are. For example, is_pinned() lacked a stable equivalent during the migration. Thankfully, there is a general-purpose torch_call_dispatcher C shim that allows us to

items.title: Maggie Appleton: Agentic Coding Has Outgrown the Text Box
items.summary:
Agentic coding has outgrown the text box. Maggie Appleton, staff research engineer at GitHub Next, argues that walls of CLI output and AGENTS.md files serve coding agents far better than the humans steering them. She walks through Chopin, the GitHub Next prototype where background agents turn a team's planning chat into a structured plan, and makes the case for agents that prompt you instead of waiting to be prompted.

What we cover:
– Why text-heavy agentic coding tools favor agents over humans
– Boundary objects: what AGENTS.md, skill files and MCP servers get right and wrong
– Multiplayer planning with coding agents in GitHub Next's Chopin
– Human-to-agent handoffs, formal verification and spec-driven development
– Why software quality is rising, not falling, with coding agents
– Which roles still matter: PMs, designers and engineers

00:02:14 - Inside GitHub Next and the Chopin project

items.title: claude-code v2.1.318
items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added a record of your answer when Claude Code asks to turn on the mods it writes in a session
  • Added assume_role on mantle upstreams of the Claude apps gateway, for a role in another AWS account and for per-developer AWS cost attribution
  • Added an effort option to a mod's $.model.fork, so a quick side job can run at low whatever effort the session uses; the result reports the effort sent
  • Added the date a stored claude.ai sign-in ends to claude auth status (loginExpiresAt) and to claude -p JSON results (credential_expires_at)
  • Added a one-line stderr warning to claude -p text output, starting 10 days before a stored claude.ai sign-in ends
  • Fixed --continue sometimes losing the earlier conversation after a malformed tool call's retries ran out (regression in 2.1.314)
  • Fixed macOS sessions with many running Bash commands stalling while memory grew
  • Fixed permission prompts being answered by keys typed just after sending a message, or before a slow prompt appeared
  • Fixed /logout, claude auth logout and claude mcp remove reporting success, and changes to trust, consent or MCP settings being dropped with no word, when the config file could not be updated on a shared network home directory
  • Fixed jobs exiting with Not logged in when another terminal or host signs in again to the same account and organization on the same home
  • Fixed claude mcp add and remove writing the config without its lock: they now wait for it or exit 1, though another job's save can still replace a saved server
  • Fixed claude plugin commands exiting before a slow token refresh was saved, which could sign you out on the next run
  • Fixed claude plugin validate passing a custom-named marketplace file that claude plugin marketplace add rejects
  • Fixed stdio MCP servers that exit on the version probe being re-probed on every start; a server that dies in under 3s for its own reason is also pinned to the legacy handshake for 7 days
  • Fixed sessions being refused at startup by an allowedProviders list that another login on the same machine had stored
  • Fixed idle compaction replacing a conversation with a reply that was not a summary
  • Fixed the "Now using usage credits" notice reappearing about every 30 seconds while a background subagent is running
  • Fixed custom slash commands that fail, or that only Claude can invoke, printing nothing in claude -p and SDK sessions
  • Fixed claude -p and Agent SDK sessions reporting success when an API error cut off a reply while a mod hooked turn.step
  • Fixed a message sent right after a model change still running after Stop in headless sessions: Stop now cancels or stops it as it would a queued message
  • Fixed a deleted session transcript being re-created with its last prompt when an idle non-interactive session exited
  • Fixed claude remote-control hosts, the background daemon and self-hosted runners failing to start new sessions (spawn ENOENT) after an update or version cleanup removed the binary of a still-running process
  • Fixed a running Claude Code process owned by another user (for example one left by sudo claude) being treated as dead by version cleanup, which could delete its binary
  • Fixed /remote-control showing a session as available after a failed connection
  • Fixed /design revoke reporting success when the request failed with a 404
  • Fixed a shell command approved after a self-hosted runner or cloud session restart running in the session's start folder, not the folder it was asked in; if that folder can't be entered, it is not run
  • Fixed Claude not being told when an approved connector tool was unavailable after a cloud session restart
  • Fixed cloud sessions being stopped in the middle of a turn when the service refuses uploads for several minutes
  • Fixed variables a Setup hook writes to CLAUDE_ENV_FILE not reaching the Bash tool in some cloud sessions
  • Fixed the iPhone app showing a cloud session's turn as finished while it kept running, after a response was cut off at a tool call or a refused image or document was removed
  • Fixed a restarted session re-sending a message that failed with an API error, ahead of the newer message waiting behind it
  • Fixed a restarted session dropping its interrupted turn when the restart came right after Claude read a large image or retried a tool call
  • Fixed every connection failing when the NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS file is empty, not PEM, or starts with a damaged certificate: readable certificates are now used, with a warning on stderr
  • Fixed workflows re-running finished agents when resumed after a usage limit
  • Fixed /mcp in cloud sessions counting tools the model can't use; a server's row now shows how many of its tools are available
  • Fixed a duplicate notification when Claude left the status field out of a PushNotification call
  • Fixed the error for a too-large image in a request with more than 20 images always saying the limit was 2000px; it now shows the API's limit
  • Fixed the runtime in background shell details not updating while the dialog is open
  • Fixed a mod's turn.step hook making a stopped reply finish as a success in headless runs
  • Fixed retention cleanup leaving a home that only runs claude -p with no ~/.claude.json backup: it now takes a fresh backup before deleting the last good one
  • Fixed the stored login being replaced by an empty file when a network home directory has no room left for data but still takes new files
  • Fixed tokens from setup-token being refused at start on machines with forceLoginOrgUUID, when the token belongs to a permitted organization
  • Fixed non-interactive launches replacing a ~/.claude.json that isn't valid JSON with defaults; the start now fails, says how to restore the file, and leaves it as is (#87551)
  • Fixed an empty ~/.claude.json with no backup being reported as corrupted; Claude Code now starts as it does when the file is missing
  • Fixed the restore command printed for a damaged or missing ~/.claude.json naming an empty or cut-off backup, or failing on a read-only file
  • Fixed the sign-in failure when a stored claude.ai login reaches its time limit: it now says so, and in claude -p names claude auth login and claude setup-token
  • Improved how ~/.claude.json, settings files and the stored login survive saves on shared network home directories: they are less often deleted, briefly emptied or replaced by a near-empty or older copy
  • Improved sessions on network file systems to look again when the configuration file is wrongly reported as missing, so fewer start without your MCP servers and trusted folders
  • Improved MCP tool errors: a call made before the tool is loaded now returns its input schema
  • Improved the reliability of git commits and pull request creation when the Bash tool runs macOS's built-in /bin/bash
  • Improved "Ask your admin for more usage" in the usage limit menu to send the request in one step
  • Improved how fast remote sessions reconnect after a pause or sleep
  • Improved You should know toasts to say "try again" instead of "press 2", which only works in the terminal
  • Improved auto-update reliability: a brief network failure while verifying a release is now retried right away instead of waiting for the next check
  • Improved unattended runs (claude -p, SDK apps) to stop rewriting ~/.claude.json on every run when nothing in it changed
  • Changed Claude Code to no longer install or update the IDE extension when started in an IDE terminal; use /ide from an outside terminal or your editor's extensions view
  • Changed subagents to stop instead of switching models when "Switch models when a message is flagged" is set to "Ask each time"
  • Changed background subagents to move a shell command to the background after 3 minutes on all providers, so the prompt cache doesn't expire while it runs
  • Changed subagent progress summaries on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or with telemetry off: on a cold prompt cache, one can now wait up to 5 minutes for the subagent's pending response
  • Changed what a mod attaches at prompt.submit to stay in the user's turn rather than go out as a system message
  • Changed deniedMcpServers URL entries to also block Anthropic-provided servers whose upstream URL matches, and connectors in cloud sessions and on self-hosted runners, where the session is given the connector's own URL; otherwise deny a connector by name
  • Changed the /permissions rule details, built-in rules and delete confirmation views to use the standard dialog; pressing Ctrl+C twice there now goes back or cancels instead of quitting
  • Changed /claude-api managed-agents-onboard to give a new agent's built-in tools, and a quickstart template's MCP tools, the auto permission policy ("Judge risky actions") by default, matching the Claude Console; say "run without asking" to opt out
  • Removed the 2.1.288 fix that kept the model's earlier thinking when resuming a conversation started on 2.1.286 or earlier; that thinking can now be dropped
  • Gateway: Added a log warning when the Google access token from a federation (external_account) credentials file is about to expire
  • Gateway: Improved the log hints about listen.trusted_proxies: they now say to list only a proxy that adds the connecting address to X-Forwarded-For itself
  • Gateway: Improved the warning when AWS CountTokens fails on Amazon Bedrock: it says Claude Code, not the gateway, counts after the 501, and points at IAM only when AWS denies access
  • Self-hosted runner: Added CLAUDE_RUNNER_SPAWN_REASON to the orchestrator's spawn-runner hook environment: why Anthropic sent the request (e.g. runner_lost, resumed); unset when none was sent
  • Self-hosted runner: Added a startup warning when --release-idle-session-min is the last argument with no value (still ignored) or has a value of only spaces (still read as 0)
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed the orchestrator's log lines: ok session=… now prints at every log level on stdout (was debug only, stderr) with reason=… after jti=…, and nack session=… ends its fields with reason=… after retryable=…; update scripts that match retryable=true: or retryable=false:
  • Remote Control: Fixed a misleading "spawn error: ENOENT" when a session's working folder is missing; the error now names the folder
  • Remote Control: Improved the title a fork of a terminal fork is created with when the app doesn't set one: "Name (fork 2)"
  • [VSCode] Fixed a window whose sign-in the organization's settings refuse starting a new Claude Code process in the background every minute
  • [VSCode] Fixed a long word in the chat panel's error banner pushing its close button out of view
  • [VSCode] Improved the sign-in screen to show what Claude Code printed when its sign-in status check fails
  • [Cloud sessions] Added a No repository option: a cloud session on an Anthropic-hosted environment can now start without picking a repository
  • [Cloud sessions] Added the usual Chrome names to cloud sessions, so tools other than Playwright can find the built-in Chromium through google-chrome and CHROME_PATH
  • [Cloud sessions] Added a New session button to the card shown when a cloud session's environment was deleted, where the message box is hidden
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed reading GitHub Actions logs in cloud sessions: gh run view --log and gh api log requests now get the log in most environments, not an unreachable redirect
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved most Create PR failure messages in cloud and Remote Control sessions: they now give the reason or a link to GitHub instead of saying Try again
  • [Cloud sessions] Changed connector search results to tell Claude that the search covers only part of the connector directory
  • [Remote Control] Fixed side-by-side checkouts of one repository looking identical in the environment menu's Remote Control rows; each now shows its own folder name
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed keyboard focus and screen reader announcements in Claude Tag admin setup; pressing Escape in the connect form no longer also closes the Add dialog
  • [Code Review] Improved the Code Review analytics page to retry once after a server or network failure, then show a Try again banner instead of empty cards
release_highlights: Added a record of your answer when Claude Code asks to turn on the mods it writes in a session
Added assume_role on mantle upstreams of the Claude apps gateway, for a role in another AWS account and for per-developer AWS cost attribution
Added an effort option to a mod's $.model.fork , so a quick side job can run at low whatever effort the session uses; the result reports the effort sent
